turns.text: please tell me explain radiology? mera bhai pooch raha hai

Radiology is the medical specialty that uses imaging to diagnose and sometimes treat disease. We use X-rays, ultrasound, CT, MRI, and nuclear medicine to look inside the body without surgery. A radiologist is a doctor trained for several years to interpret these images. Some radiologists also do minimally invasive procedures (called interventional radiology), such as biopsies, drainages, or placing stents under image guidance.
okay, and what should i avoid?
Side effects are usually mild and short-lived — we monitor closely.
What does a radiologist do? thanks

A radiologist is a medical doctor who specialises in interpreting medical images and, in some cases, performing image-guided procedures. After your scan, the radiologist reads the images, compares them with prior studies if available, and writes a report for the doctor who referred you. They do not usually meet patients directly except for interventional procedures.
also what about water?
Take it at the same time each day for consistency.
one more thing, explain the difference between an scan and a ct imaging? — dard horaha hai

CT uses X-rays to build a 3D image and is fast, widely available, and very good for bone, lung, and bleeding. MRI uses a strong magnet and radio waves (no ionising radiation) and is best for soft tissue such as brain, spinal cord, joints, and pelvis. CT typically takes a few minutes; MRI takes 20-45 minutes and is noisier. Your doctor chooses the test that answers your clinical question with the lowest risk.
explain Do I need to avoid eating before my imaging imaging? ?

For most MRI scans, fasting is not required. For abdominal or pelvic MRI with contrast, please avoid food and drink for 4 hours before. For an MRCP (bile duct scan) fasting may be longer. Check your appointment letter or call us if unsure.
Is the gadolinium contrast injection safe? thori si khansi bhi hai

Gadolinium contrast used in MRI is generally safe for healthy adults. Mild side effects can include warmth, a metallic taste, or brief nausea. Please tell us if you have kidney problems, have had a previous reaction, are pregnant, or are breastfeeding so we can review the risk and the dose.
quick question, how much time for will my ct scan take? kindly aap bata sakte hain

A typical CT scan takes 10 to 20 minutes overall. The scan itself is under a minute. Positioning, IV line placement for contrast, and breath-hold instructions add to the total time. Please arrive 15 minutes early to fill in the safety form.
quick question, When will I get my test report? kindly thori si tension hai

Routine reports are ready in 2 to 5 working days and sent to the doctor who referred you. Urgent in-patient and emergency-room scans are reported on the same day. You can request a copy at the front desk once your doctor has reviewed it with you.
okay, and what should i avoid?
If symptoms worsen, please contact the clinic or emergency line.
Can I have an imaging if I have a pacemaker? thanks thori si khansi bhi hai

Older pacemakers are not safe in an MRI. Most pacemakers fitted in the last 10 years are MRI-conditional, meaning they can be scanned with special settings. Bring your device card so the technologist can check the model. We will only proceed if your cardiology team has cleared the scan.
i was wondering Will my tattoos cause problems during an imaging? thanks

Most modern tattoo inks are safe. Some older or dark inks contain metal particles that can warm slightly during the scan. Tell the technologist if you notice any burning sensation and the scan can be paused. The risk of a serious burn is very low.
okay, and what should i avoid?
Most patients tolerate this well; tell us if anything new appears.
I am claustrophobic. How do you help during an scan?? aap bata sakte hain

Tell us before you book. We can prescribe a mild sedative to take an hour before, play music through headphones, offer an eye mask, and let a family member stay in the room. Open or wide-bore MRI machines are an option for some scans. Most patients complete the scan with these supports.
okay, and what should i avoid?
Driving is usually fine unless you were given a sedative.
explain Will the test hurt? ? thori si khansi bhi hai

MRI, CT, X-ray, and ultrasound scans are painless. You may feel a brief pinch when an IV line is placed for contrast. Some patients find it uncomfortable to lie still for long periods, especially for MRI. Tell the technologist if you have back pain so we can use a cushion.
tell me is it okay to eat prior to a chest x-ray? mera bhai pooch raha hai

Yes. There is no fasting requirement for plain X-rays, including chest, spine, and limb X-rays. Eat and drink as normal and take your usual medicines. You will be asked to remove clothing and metal jewelry from the area being imaged.
tell me Is the radiation from a ct scan test dangerous? please

CT uses ionising radiation, but the dose is kept as low as possible and modern scanners are highly optimised. A single CT chest is about the same as 2 years of background radiation. The benefit of a clear diagnosis usually outweighs the small added risk. We do not scan unless it is clinically justified.
i need to know Can I have a imaging if I am pregnant? plz

MRI and ultrasound are generally safe in pregnancy and are preferred when imaging is needed. X-ray and CT use ionising radiation and are avoided unless absolutely required, in which case the abdomen is shielded. Please tell the technologist if you are or might be pregnant before any scan.
is it serious?
Driving is usually fine unless you were given a sedative.
please tell me What should I wear for the scan? thori si khansi bhi hai

Wear comfortable, loose clothing without metal fasteners, zips, or buttons. For most scans you will be given a hospital gown to change into. Leave jewelry and watches at home. Sports bras with metal underwires are not allowed in the MRI room.
could you tell me Do I need someone to drive me home post the imaging? please

If you received only an MRI, CT, X-ray, or ultrasound, you can drive yourself home. If you took a sedative for claustrophobia or had an interventional procedure such as a biopsy, please arrange a driver. The receptionist can confirm what applies to your appointment.
is it safe for kids?
It is generally safe but please review with your physician for your case.
What is the difference between imaging and computed tomography? ? — dard horaha hai

MRI uses a magnetic field and radio waves and produces detailed images of soft tissue. CT uses X-rays and produces fast cross-sectional images, especially good for bones, lungs, and emergencies. Your doctor chooses based on the body part and the question being asked.
quick question, Can my child come into the test room with me?? thori si tension hai

Children under 12 are generally not allowed inside the MRI scan room for safety. They are welcome in the waiting area with another adult. For CT and X-ray rooms a child may sit outside the door with the technologist's permission. Please arrange child care if possible.
explain how much time for does an scan take? thanks in advance thori si khansi bhi hai

A typical MRI takes 20 to 45 minutes depending on the body part and the number of sequences. Brain and spine scans are around 30 minutes. Full-body scans can take over an hour. We will tell you the expected duration when you arrive.
quick question, Why must I remove all my jewelry? thanks

Metal items are pulled strongly by the MRI magnet and can become dangerous projectiles. Even small items can heat up or distort the image. Earrings, watches, body piercings, hair pins, and rings must all be removed before entering the MRI room.
how soon should i come back?
If symptoms worsen, please contact the clinic or emergency line.
can you tell me Will I be alone inside the imaging scanner??

You will be inside the scanner alone, but the technologist watches you on camera the whole time. You hold a panic button you can press if you need to come out, and you can hear the technologist through headphones. They will check on you between sequences.
can you tell me is it advisable to take my regular medicines before the test? aap bata sakte hain

Yes, take all your routine medicines unless you have been told otherwise. The exception is metformin (a diabetes pill), which is sometimes paused for CT scans with contrast. Bring a list of your medicines to the appointment.
what if it gets worse?
Most of the work is included in your normal appointment fee.
explain What if I am allergic to iodine contrast? thori si tension hai

Tell us at booking and again on arrival. If your reaction was mild (rash, itching) we can pre-medicate you with steroids and antihistamines. If the reaction was severe (breathing difficulty, swelling) we will avoid iodine contrast and use a different test such as MRI or ultrasound.
thanks, just one more — is it safe in pregnancy?
We address that on the FAQ page; ask if you want details.
am i allowed to breastfeed post i receive contrast? plz — dard horaha hai

Yes. The amount of iodine or gadolinium contrast that passes into breast milk and is absorbed by the baby is extremely small. International guidelines say it is safe to continue breastfeeding as normal. If you prefer, you can pump and discard for 12 to 24 hours.
how soon should i come back?
Most of the work is included in your normal appointment fee.
kindly explain What is the difference between ultrasound and X-ray?

Ultrasound uses sound waves, has no radiation, and is best for soft tissue and pregnancy. X-ray uses ionising radiation and is best for bones and chest. Ultrasound is real-time, while X-ray is a single snapshot. Each is suited to different questions.
any side effects?
Children may need a different dose or protocol — ask the paediatric team.
tell me Why do I need a full bladder for a pelvic ultrasound??

A full bladder pushes the bowel out of the way and acts as a window for the sound waves, giving clearer images of the uterus, ovaries, or prostate. Drink 4 to 6 glasses of water about an hour before the scan and do not empty your bladder until told.
i was wondering How loud is the MRI machine? plz aap bata sakte hain

MRI machines are loud, from 80 to 110 decibels, similar to standing near heavy traffic. We provide earplugs and headphones, and you can listen to music. The noise is a normal part of the imaging and does not mean anything is wrong.
i need to know Will iodine contrast harm my kidneys?

For people with normal kidney function the risk is very small. For people with reduced kidney function (eGFR below 30) the risk is higher and we usually choose a different test. We will check your blood test before scanning if needed.
what if it gets worse?
It is generally safe but please review with your physician for your case.
please tell me What is a PET scan? please (urdu: dard hai)

A PET (positron emission tomography) scan uses a small dose of a radioactive sugar tracer to show areas of high metabolic activity. It is often combined with CT and is used for cancer staging and some heart and brain conditions. The whole appointment takes about 2 hours.
is it okay during ramadan?
Most patients tolerate this well; tell us if anything new appears.
do you know Can I have an MRI with metal implants in my body? — dard horaha hai

Most modern orthopaedic implants such as plates, screws, and joint replacements are safe in MRI. We will check the model and date of any implant against an MRI safety database. Some cochlear implants, certain neurostimulators, and old aneurysm clips are not safe and we will offer an alternative.
can you tell me Do I need a referral to book a scan? please

Yes, a referral from a doctor is required for every diagnostic imaging exam. The referral makes sure the right test is chosen and that the report is sent back to the right person. We accept referrals from GPs, specialists, and emergency departments.
i was wondering how early do i need to arrive for my test? ? thori si tension hai

Please arrive 15 minutes before the appointment for X-ray and ultrasound, and 30 minutes early for CT, MRI, or any scan with contrast. This gives time for paperwork, the safety questionnaire, IV line placement, and changing into a gown.
can i drive after that?
We address that on the FAQ page; ask if you want details.
kindly explain Will someone explain the procedure before it starts? thori si tension hai

Yes. The radiographer or technologist will explain every step, the body position, breath-hold cues, and the noises you will hear. You can ask questions at any time. The radiologist (specialist doctor) is also available if you have clinical concerns about the scan.
should i be worried?
Good follow-up — please discuss the specifics with your clinician at the next visit.
i want to know How is an ultrasound performed?? thori si tension hai

A gel is applied to the area being scanned and a small handheld probe is moved over the skin. The probe sends and receives high-frequency sound waves and the computer builds a live image. It is painless, uses no radiation, and takes 15-30 minutes. You may be asked to drink water beforehand for a pelvic scan, or fast for an abdominal scan.
is it safe for kids?
Side effects are usually mild and short-lived — we monitor closely.
one more thing, explain a pet-ct scan scan? ? aap bata sakte hain

A PET-CT combines a CT scan (anatomy) with a PET scan (function). A small radioactive sugar tracer is injected and areas using a lot of sugar - often tumours or infection - light up. The scan takes 30-60 minutes including a 60-minute uptake wait. Tell us if you have diabetes; we may adjust the protocol.
should i be worried?
Side effects are usually mild and short-lived — we monitor closely.
What is interventional radiology?

Interventional radiology uses imaging (ultrasound, fluoroscopy, CT) to guide minimally invasive procedures such as biopsies, drainages, angioplasty, and stent placement. Most procedures are done under local anaesthetic through a small skin nick, so recovery is faster than open surgery.
do you know Why must I remove all metal before an imaging? kindly

The MRI uses a very strong magnet. Loose metal can be pulled into the bore and cause injury, and metal on the body distorts the images. Remove jewellery, watches, hairpins, coins, and metal-rimmed glasses. Tell us in advance about implants, pacemakers, cochlear devices, or recent surgery with clips.
what if i forget once?
We address that on the FAQ page; ask if you want details.
please tell me How much radiation does a ct scan scan use? aap bata sakte hain

A typical chest CT delivers about 7 mSv, similar to 2-3 years of natural background radiation. A head CT is around 2 mSv. The benefit of a needed scan greatly outweighs the small risk, but we still use the lowest dose that gives a diagnostic image.
thanks, just one more — is it safe in pregnancy?
We address that on the FAQ page; ask if you want details.
i need to konw Can I drive post a contrast test? kindly

Yes, you can drive immediately after most contrast scans. If you were given a sedative for claustrophobia, do not drive for 24 hours. If you feel light-headed or unwell after contrast, wait until you feel normal and tell our staff.
is it expensive?
Side effects are usually mild and short-lived — we monitor closely.
define a boen-density scan (dexa)??

DEXA uses a very low dose of X-rays to measure how dense your bones are at the hip and spine. The scan takes about 10 minutes, is painless, and you stay fully clothed (no metal). We use the result to assess osteoporosis risk and the need for treatment.
can i drive after that?
Driving is usually fine unless you were given a sedative.
What is a fluoroscopy? thori si khansi hbi hai

Fluoroscopy is a real-time moving X-ray, used to watch swallowing, bowel motion, or to guide a needle into a joint. The exam takes 10-30 minutes. You may be asked to drink contrast (barium) or have it injected, depending on the test.
my report says 'incidental finding' - do i need to be worried? thanks in advance (urdu: dard hai)

Incidental findings are things picked up by chance that were not the reason for the scan. Most are benign (cysts, small nodules, age-related changes) and only need observation. Your referring doctor will explain whether the finding needs any follow-up imaging or testing.
could you tell me Will the radiology team discuss my results with me?

Radiologists send a written report to your referring doctor, who will discuss results with you in context. For interventional procedures the radiologist will speak with you directly before and after. If you have questions about the report itself, your referring doctor can request a clarification.
quick question, Why do I have to hold my breath during a imaging?...

Holding your breath stops the chest and upper abdomen from moving, which makes the image sharper. We will guide you with a recording or hand signals - usually 10-20 seconds for CT and slightly longer for MRI. Practice slow deep breaths before the scan to make it easier.
and how often?
Children may need a different dose or protocol — ask the paediatric team.
one more thing, What is the gadolinium contrast and when do you use it??

Gadolinium is a contrast agent used in MRI to highlight blood vessels, inflammation, and tumours. It is given through a small IV cannula. It is safe for most patients but is avoided in advanced kidney disease and used cautiously in pregnancy.
and how often?
Side effects are usually mild and short-lived — we monitor closely.
explain my child is having an mri - what do i need to expect? kindly aap bata sakte hain

Young children may need a feed-and-sleep protocol or light sedation to lie still. Bring favourite blankets, dummies, and a change of clothes. We will explain everything to you and your child, and one parent can usually stay in the scan room.
what if i forget once?
Good follow-up — please discuss the specifics with your clinician at the next visit.
am i allowed to keep my insulin pump on during the test? plz — dard horaha hai

Insulin pumps must be removed and kept outside the MRI room as they contain metal and electronics. For a CT it is usually fine to keep the pump on, but tell the technologist so they can avoid the device in the field of view.
thanks, just one more — is it safe in pregnancy?
Most of the work is included in your normal appointment fee.
could you explain is it okay to have an imaging with metal implants?... — dard horaha hai

Most modern orthopaedic implants (knee, hip, plates, screws) are MRI-safe but produce some local image distortion. Tell us in advance and bring the implant card if possible. Cochlear implants, some neurostimulators, and very old aneurysm clips are usually not safe - we will discuss alternatives such as CT or ultrasound.
is it okay during ramadan?
Good follow-up — please discuss the specifics with your clinician at the next visit.
could you tell me Is the contrast dye injection painful? thanks in advance (urdu: dard hai)

You will feel a quick pinch when the cannula is inserted, similar to a blood test. Once the dye flows you may feel a warm flush, a metallic taste, or a brief feeling of needing to pass urine - these are normal and pass within seconds.
i need to know Can my partner stay with me during a imaging? please mera bhai pooch raha hai

For CT, MRI and most X-ray exams the room must be kept clear during the actual scan. A partner can wait in the changing area and may step in afterwards. For ultrasound a companion can often stay in the room - just ask the sonographer.
i need to know What is a ventilation-perfusion (V/Q) test?

A V/Q scan checks airflow (ventilation) and blood flow (perfusion) to the lungs using two small radioactive tracers, one inhaled and one injected. It is the test of choice for suspected pulmonary embolism in pregnant patients because it gives less foetal radiation than a CT angiogram.
i was wondering My X-ray report mentions a 'nodule'. What does that mean? aap bata sakte hain

A nodule is a small rounded spot, usually less than 30 mm. Most lung nodules are benign (old infection, scar tissue). The radiologist follows a published schedule for surveillance imaging based on the nodule's size and your smoking history. Your referring doctor will explain whether any follow-up is needed.
one more thing, Why is there a long wait between booking and my test? please

Demand for MRI and CT is high, and certain protocols (cardiac MRI, MRCP, paediatric sedation) need specialist staff. We triage urgent cases (suspected cancer, post-op review) ahead of routine work. If you become more symptomatic while waiting, ask your referring doctor to mark the request as urgent.
quick question, Can I drink water before an abdominal ultrasound?... — dard horaha hai

For a regular abdominal scan, please fast 6 hours so we can see the gallbladder clearly. For a pelvic or bladder scan, finish a litre of water in the hour before the appointment and arrive with a full bladder - it acts as an acoustic window.
what if it gets worse?
Most of the work is included in your normal appointment fee.
what about this — What is a CT-guided biopsy? plz — dard horaha hai

A CT-guided biopsy uses real-time CT imaging to place a fine needle precisely into an abnormal area to take a tissue sample. It is done under local anaesthetic, takes 30-60 minutes, and you go home the same day. Mild bruising and a small risk of bleeding are the main side effects.
is it safe for kids?
Driving is usually fine unless you were given a sedative.
Do I need a chaperone for my scan? thanks in advance

You are welcome to ask for a chaperone for any examination, especially scans that involve the chest, breast, abdomen, or pelvis. Just tell reception when you arrive and one will be arranged free of charge.
can you tell me Will my scan report be sent to my GP?... thori si khansi bhi hai

Yes - the radiologist's report is sent automatically to the doctor who referred you, who will discuss the result with you at your next appointment. You can request your own copy by writing to the radiology department.
is there a home remedy?
If symptoms worsen, please contact the clinic or emergency line.
tell me What is a mammogram and who needs one? kindly

A mammogram is a low-dose X-ray of the breast used to screen for early breast cancer. Routine screening usually begins at age 40-50 depending on local guidelines and family history, repeating every 1-2 years. Tell us about previous breast surgery, implants, or current breastfeeding. The exam takes 15-20 minutes; brief compression is normal.
is it okay during ramadan?
Side effects are usually mild and short-lived — we monitor closely.
kindly explain define paediatric scan sedation and when is it needed? ?

Children under 6 often cannot stay still for a full MRI. We offer 'feed-and-sleep' for babies, child-life play preparation for older children, and light sedation when needed. An anaesthetist is present for any sedation. Fasting times are: 6 hours for solids, 4 hours for breast milk, 2 hours for clear fluids.
Can I have an scan during my period? plz thori si tension hai

Yes - there is no medical reason to delay an MRI because of menstruation. Wear comfortable clothing and use a sanitary pad rather than a tampon if asked to change into a gown. For pelvic MRI we may ask you to schedule on specific cycle days.
is it safe for kids?
It is generally safe but please review with your physician for your case.
can you tell me Why do I feel a warm rush during contrast injection? thanks in advance

Iodine contrast can cause a warm flush spreading from the arm through the body, plus a metallic taste or a brief sensation of needing to urinate. This is a normal reaction lasting under 30 seconds and is not an allergy. Tell us if it persists, becomes painful, or if you develop a rash or breathlessness.
explain define a swallow study (barium swallow)? aap bata sakte hain

A barium swallow uses live X-ray to watch how you swallow a chalky liquid (barium). It is used to diagnose reflux, hiatal hernia, achalasia, and swallowing difficulty. Takes 15-30 minutes; you must fast 4-6 hours beforehand. Barium turns the stool white for 1-3 days afterwards - this is harmless.
should i be worried?
Side effects are usually mild and short-lived — we monitor closely.
What is a ct scan angiogram?

A CT angiogram (CTA) uses iodine contrast and a fast CT scan to image arteries - most commonly the coronary, pulmonary, brain, or abdominal arteries. Useful for chest pain, suspected pulmonary embolism, and stroke. Bring kidney-function blood tests and tell us if you take metformin.
is it expensive?
Most patients tolerate this well; tell us if anything new appears.
tell me am i allowed to have a test if i have a metallic foreign body in my eye? thanks in advance thori si khansi bhi hai

Tell us before MRI booking - we routinely screen welders and metal-workers. A history of metallic eye injury is checked with a quick orbital X-ray. If a metal fragment is present we use CT instead. There is no risk for CT, ultrasound, or X-ray.
also what about water?
We address that on the FAQ page; ask if you want details.
i was wondering tell me about the difference between a screening and a diagnostic mammogram? ? aap bata sakte hain

Screening mammograms are routine, brief, and done in asymptomatic women on a regular schedule. Diagnostic mammograms use additional views, magnification, or ultrasound to investigate a lump, pain, or an abnormal screening result. Diagnostic appointments take longer and the radiologist may discuss findings on the spot.
what about this — How is a thyroid ultrasound done? thori si khansi bhi hai

You lie on your back with a pillow under your shoulders to extend the neck. A gel and small probe slide over the front of the neck for 15-20 minutes. It is painless, uses no radiation, and visualises nodules, cysts, and lymph nodes. No fasting needed.
also what about water?
It is generally safe but please review with your physician for your case.
quick question, What is an interventional radiology drainage?? mera bhai pooch raha hai

An image-guided drainage uses ultrasound or CT to place a small tube through the skin into a collection of fluid (abscess, bile, urine) so it can drain externally. Done under local anaesthetic with sedation; the tube stays in for days to weeks while the cavity heals.
is it expensive?
Most patients tolerate this well; tell us if anything new appears.
explain Why is my appointment letter so detailed about jewellery?... thori si khansi bhi hai

MRI uses a 1.5 or 3 Tesla magnet that can pull ferromagnetic items into the scanner at high speed, causing injury and image distortion. Hair clips, body piercings, watches, and underwire bras all need to come off. Plain gold and platinum are usually safe but we still ask you to remove them so we get the cleanest image.
also what about water?
If symptoms worsen, please contact the clinic or emergency line.
could you explain How long does an MRCP take? please thori si tension hai

MRCP (magnetic resonance cholangio-pancreatography) is a special MRI of the bile and pancreatic ducts. It takes 30-45 minutes, uses no contrast, and requires 4-6 hours of fasting so the bile ducts dilate clearly. Drink a small amount of pineapple or blueberry juice on arrival - natural manganese darkens the stomach.
What is bone scintigraphy? thanks

A bone scan injects a small dose of radioactive tracer that concentrates in areas of high bone turnover (fractures, infection, tumours). You wait 2-3 hours after injection for the tracer to settle, then the scan itself takes 30-45 minutes. The tracer is cleared in 24 hours; drink plenty of water.
Are scans safe during the first trimester of pregnancy? kindly thori si khansi bhi hai

Ultrasound is the safest imaging in pregnancy and is the first choice. MRI without contrast is also considered safe but is usually avoided in the first trimester unless urgent. CT and conventional X-ray expose the foetus to ionising radiation and are avoided unless there is no alternative.
could you explain What happens to my old scans? ?

Images are archived securely in our PACS (Picture Archiving and Communication System) for 7-10 years, or longer for paediatric and oncology studies. You can request copies on CD or via secure online transfer. Old films from the pre-digital era may be in long-term storage and take longer to retrieve.
i was wondering What is physiotherapy? ? — dard horaha hai

Physiotherapy (also called physical therapy) is the use of exercise, manual treatment, and education to restore movement and reduce pain. It is non-surgical and drug-free. A physiotherapist assesses how your joints, muscles, and nerves are working, finds the cause of the problem, and gives you a tailored plan. Common reasons people see us include back and neck pain, sports injuries, post-surgery rehab, stroke recovery, and conditions such as arthritis or sciatica.
any side effects?
Take it at the same time each day for consistency.
what about this — What does a physiotherapist do? mera bhai pooch raha hai

A physiotherapist is a healthcare professional trained to evaluate movement problems and treat them with exercise, manual therapy (hands-on techniques), and education. They build a personalised programme for you, teach you home exercises, track your progress, and refer you on if imaging or medical review is needed. They do not prescribe medicines.
should i be worried?
Most of the work is included in your normal appointment fee.
tell me What conditions can physiotherapy help with? (urdu: dard hai)

Physiotherapy helps with a wide range of issues: muscle and joint pain (back, neck, knee, shoulder), sports injuries, post-fracture or post-surgery recovery, sciatica, frozen shoulder, plantar fasciitis, arthritis, balance and falls in older adults, and rehab after a stroke or heart attack. If your problem is mostly mechanical (worse with movement, better with rest or specific positions), physiotherapy is usually the first-line treatment.
is it safe for kids?
Driving is usually fine unless you were given a sedative.
could you explain frequency of should i do my home exercises? plz

Most home exercise programmes work best when done once or twice a day, 4 to 5 days a week. Stick to the reps and sets your physiotherapist gave you and stop if you feel sharp pain. Consistency matters more than intensity, especially in the first two weeks.
what if it gets worse?
Side effects are usually mild and short-lived — we monitor closely.
please tell me Is it normal to feel sore after a session?

Mild soreness for 24 to 48 hours after a session is normal, especially in the first few weeks. Sharp pain, swelling that does not settle, or pain that wakes you at night is not. Contact your physiotherapist if soreness is severe or lasts more than 3 days.
i was wondering How many physiotherapy sessions will I need? thanks aap bata sakte hain

It depends on the condition. Most patients see meaningful change within 6 to 12 sessions. Acute injuries may need fewer, chronic problems often need more. Your physiotherapist will review your progress every 4 to 6 sessions and adjust the plan.
is it expensive?
Driving is usually fine unless you were given a sedative.
could you tell me when is it okay to return to running post an injury? thanks

Generally when you can walk briskly without pain, hop on the affected leg ten times, and complete your prescribed strength exercises pain-free. Start with a walk-jog programme of 1 minute jog and 2 minutes walk. Increase gradually by no more than 10% per week.
is there a home remedy?
It is generally safe but please review with your physician for your case.
i need to know What should I bring to my first physiotherapy session? plz

Bring any referral letter, recent scan or X-ray reports, a list of current medicines, and comfortable clothing you can move in. Loose shorts or leggings and a t-shirt work best. Allow 45 to 60 minutes for the first visit.
i need to know what is it advisable to wear to a physiotherapy session? ?

Wear loose, comfortable clothing that allows free movement and access to the area we are treating. Shorts for knee or hip work, a t-shirt or vest for shoulder work. Bring trainers if we are doing balance or running drills. Avoid jeans.
explain What is the difference between heat and ice for an injury?...

Ice (cold therapy) is for new injuries in the first 48 to 72 hours to reduce swelling and pain. Heat is for stiff, tight muscles and chronic aches to relax tissue and improve blood flow. If unsure, ice fresh injuries and heat older problems.
is it safe for kids?
Most patients tolerate this well; tell us if anything new appears.
explain How long should I ice an injury? please

Apply ice for 15 to 20 minutes at a time, with at least an hour between sessions, for the first 48 to 72 hours. Use a thin towel between the ice pack and your skin to prevent ice burn. Do not sleep on an ice pack.
what if it gets worse?
It is generally safe but please review with your physician for your case.
could you explain is bed rest good for sore back? please mera bhai pooch raha hai

No. Modern evidence shows long bed rest delays recovery and weakens muscles. Stay as active as the pain allows, walk regularly, and avoid lying down for more than a few hours. Most acute back pain settles within 6 weeks with gentle movement.
define sciatica?? thori si khansi hbi hai

Sciatica is pain that radiates down the back of the leg, usually from irritation of the sciatic nerve in the lower back. Common causes are a disc bulge or tight muscles pressing on the nerve. Most cases improve within 6 to 12 weeks with exercise and posture work.
what if i forget once?
